verdict.rationale: OpenRouter's model-fallback and load-balancing routing explicitly handles provider rate-limits by trying other providers/models automatically (docs-3, docs-19, docs-38, docs-4), and its key-management API lets engineers programmatically create/rotate/distribute keys (docs-8), while BYOK gives direct control over provider-side rate limits (docs-9/24/32). However there is no explicit documented request-queuing or client-side throttling mechanism, and 'spreading traffic across keys' is only supported via generic key-management APIs rather than a built-in load-balancing-across-keys feature. missing for 10: explicit request queuing/throttling controls, native multi-key traffic distribution feature, independent verification that key rotation smooths rate limits in practice.
